name: Halftone Converter
role: Python CLI that renders stills as halftone screens with set angles per CMYK plate
summary: Python CLI `halftonecv` (and library) that redraws a raster as Cairo-drawn round-dot halftones in gray, RGB or CMYK, with pitch, scale, blur and per-channel screen angles, using ICC profiles for the colour conversion. Stills only; one process per frame.
use_when: A print-process look needs real per-plate screen angles (CMYK 15, 75, 0, 45) rather than a filter approximation
Treating a still asset before it enters a scene
avoid_when: Quick ordered-dither or threshold looks: imagemagick
Distributed code that must not be AGPL: call it as a CLI only
Per-frame video treatment where a shader or filter is cheaper

install.macos: python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install halftone-converter==2.6.14

notes: 2026-11-27: The lead's CLI entry point was unverified; it is `halftonecv` (also `python -m halftonecv`), not `halftone-converter`.

2026-11-27: `-o cmyk` writes the rendered image as a TIFF, not separated plates. Only dots of the C plate show on saturated red, since M and Y saturate; use mid-tone inputs. Isolate a plate with `--keep-*` on the others.

assessment.rationale: PyPI 2.6.14 uploaded 2026-11-10 (33 releases since 2023), AGPL-3.0-or-later in wheel metadata, 42 stars, one maintainer. imagemagick and g-mic can fake halftones with dither or filters; none sets a rotated screen angle per CMYK plate with ICC conversion. Niche, so keep and do not promote.

evidence.result: 13 checks pass, repeat identical: gray at -A 45 measures 45.0 deg, period 15.74 px (pitch 8, scale 2); CMYK plates isolated with --keep-* measure C 14.5, M 75.5, Y 0.0, K 45.0 deg for 15/75/0/45; gray output byte-identical on repeat.
evidence.scope: Screen angle, pitch and determinism on flat patches, default SWOP profile; not ICC accuracy, photos, video frames or other platforms; macOS arm64, Python 3.12.
